original_card.question: Can a decoder deliver the local paid mass in fewer, larger-rank children (block frame climbs instead of rank-1 to rank-3 steps)?
methods: Find one exact small decoding identity whose frame path climbs in blocks, and price its complete per-call profile.
Bound the best effective child rank achievable for one fixed support alphabet, including copies, frames and restoration.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A per-call local profile, with all copied information, frames and restoration counted, whose ceiling exceeds the selected word's by at least 5%; masked or overcomplete supports must change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin. Ideal budget: rank-16 delivery is 2.31x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: Rank-1 children are about half of recursive cost; the selected word's effective child rank is about 3.9. Larger-rank delivery lowers recursive cost per unit of paid mass.
allowed_variations: One masked, overcomplete or block decoder family with exact labels and supports.
A scoped lower bound on effective rank for one alphabet.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Repacking idle remainders of an unchanged word (covered by the packing ceiling).
Repeating the eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.

actual_scope: Selected complex word only: replace f disjoint pairs of rank-1 paid children by f rank-2 paid children per call, preserving local mass; optionally add h rank-1 paid children, displacing h units of idle mass. Retain the nine-stage 896-family template, 64 centre charge, coverage law, rank-51 idle guard, and all other paid children. Certify the integer threshold for a 5% improvement of the baseline ideal kappa ceiling.
scope_change_reason: The original card asks for a physically priced block decoder. This package is a conditional idle-substitution cost screen with no decoder. After completion, cached overlap showed PR1605 already gives the broader rank-2..51 integer reblocking screen with on-top overhead; this package is retained only as a narrow complementary bookkeeping handoff, not proposed as a new PR.
bottleneck_link: At fixed coverage law the binding complex side needs substantially fewer small-rank recursive children. The exact screen shows that a few pair fusions cannot move the ideal packing ceiling by 5%.
stop_rule: Stop after exact boundary checks for free pair fusions and rank-1 overhead at all possible fusions; do not infer physical feasibility.
evidence: RESULT.json, source-bound exact interval verifier: 721 pair fusions fail the +5% ideal-ceiling target, 722 pass its relaxation; at 1206 fusions 171 added rank-1 children pass and 172 fail. Passing is only optimistic model feasibility. PR1605 head 488f2ecf already covers the broader no-overhead block-rank question; this note changes the target from primitive saving to kappa and lets added rank-1 work displace idle mass.
author: Josie Elliston
ai_assistance: Substantial assistance from OpenAI Codex (GPT-6): task refinement, arithmetic experiment, verifier and write-up. Account holder Josie Elliston is credited as submitter; no independent human review.

open_questions.question: Can a concrete changed decoder or frame path realize at least 722 mass-preserving rank-1 pair fusions per call with fewer than its remaining cost margin in extra paid children?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the first rank-2-only profile in this narrow model whose ideal packing ceiling reaches the 5% target.
open_questions.first_step: Find two compatible rank-1 transitions in the pinned selected word, state their dirty-state and frame contract, and build one exact local replacement before scaling.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package supplies no compatible-pair census or physical fusion; historical coalescing examples change different words.

open_questions.question: Can a different paid-rank reshaping, centre path, or coverage law meet the target with fewer local changes?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The 722 threshold applies only to pairwise rank-1-to-rank-2 replacement with all other paid children fixed.
open_questions.first_step: Write its complete optimistic per-call profile and charge centre, copied information, restoration and helper changes; screen with an applicable exact moment bound.
open_questions.blocked_by: If the template or coverage law changes, the #1240 calculator needs a replacement model.
